messages:
maria: Heads up, ran into a nasty combo on Fedora Silverblue while trying to demo redwoodctl local mode. The system has a flatpak shim in PATH and the binary from our installer in /usr/local/bin. When I run `redwoodctl login --profile=staging --localtest` the CLI sometimes hangs and then the auth step fails with a 502.

aj: Oof. Can you confirm which binary is running with `which redwoodctl` and also share the output of `redwoodctl localtest --debug`?

maria: `which` shows `/usr/bin/flatpak/exports/redwoodctl` (the shim). I forced the system binary with `env -i PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin redwoodctl version` and got the newer version.

maria: Debug run (trimmed):
```
$ redwoodctl localtest --debug
INFO starting local auth-proxy on 127.0.0.1:43120
ERROR bind: permission denied
panic: failed to start auth-proxy
```

maria: Also spotted an SELinux AVC denial immediately after the bind error in audit logs: `avc: denied { name_connect }` referencing pid of redwoodctl.

jess: That matches behavior I've seen on immutable systems: the flatpak shim can mask the real binary and SELinux/user namespace rules block binds to some ports. Two things to file: (1) better onboarding docs for Flatpak/Silverblue, (2) make localtest choose user-bindable ports and surface clearer errors about SELinux.

aj: Agreed. Quick workaround: `REDWOOD_PROFILE=` to unset env overrides and run the explicit system PATH. Also try running without the shim by invoking the absolute path. That should avoid config/profile precedence weirdness.

maria: Good tip — unsetting REDWOOD_PROFILE did fix the CLI preference issue. However, even with the system binary the local auth-proxy still failed to bind unless I temporarily setenforce 0.

tom: We shouldn't recommend setenforce 0. Instead: (A) make auth-proxy avoid privileged ports and respect user-level port ranges; (B) on bind errors add a diagnostic hint suggesting SELinux audit check commands; (C) auto-remove stale sockets in /tmp created by crashed localtest instances.

jess: I'll push a patch to try ports >= 1025 by default and to implement a 3-attempt fallback across nearby ports. Also adding code to remove stale `/tmp/redwood_localtest_*/*.sock` if they're older than 15s.

aj: There's also a UX bug where REDWOOD_PROFILE env overrides CLI flags in 1.8.x; docs claim flags should win. I'll open a fix PR and update the quickstart note.

maria: One more oddity: after a crash a leftover socket prevented restart until I manually `rm`. If we can auto-detect stale sockets and warn about ownership/SELinux rather than cryptic bind failures that would save a lot of time.

jess: Adding a clear error: "failed to bind auth-proxy: permission denied — possible causes: SELinux denial, Flatpak shim running an older binary, or stale socket under /tmp. Troubleshooting: run `env -i PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin redwoodctl login --profile=staging --localtest --verbose`, check `sudo ausearch -m avc -ts recent | tail`, and remove `/tmp/redwood_localtest_*` if present."

aj: I'll also add a short KB under Local Testing -> Silverblue/Immutable OS with those exact commands to the docs site.

tom: Plan of record: jess PR for port fallback + stale-socket cleanup (PR #4850), aj PR for env vs flag precedence fix and docs (PR #4851), small follow-up to improve the bind error message. Target: patch release tomorrow pending CI.

maria: Thanks everyone — happy to smoke-test on Silverblue once the patch drops. :thumbsup:

devex-bot: issue:created jess/localtest-port-fallback-and-cleanup -> Issue #1278

aj: If anyone else on immutable distros hits this, please react here so we can prioritize backporting to the current stable installer.
